name: Soft Currency
tagline: A product-defined currency the system grants through ordinary use rather than payment, held in a balance until it's spent.
desc: Soft currency accumulates through the product's own repeatable activity, completing something, participating over time, or receiving a recurring grant, rather than through a purchase. The units sit in a balance until the user exchanges them for something the product defines, a practice module, a cosmetic, a retry. The same balance doesn't stop being soft currency if it's also sold for money elsewhere; what matters is that a non-paid, repeatable way into the balance exists somewhere in the product.
principle: The balance accumulates before any spending decision gets made, so by the time the user chooses what to exchange it for, the currency already feels like something they have rather than something they're choosing to acquire.
warn: The distinction to hold onto is whether the units can actually be exchanged for something, or whether they only measure progress toward a threshold. A counter that only unlocks a level is progression value, not a currency, regardless of what it's called or drawn as.
variants: Activity-earned, qualifying actions or completions add units directly
Recurring-grant, the product adds units on a daily, weekly, or account-cycle rule
Restricted, spendable only inside a defined feature or area
Dual-path, the same balance can also be bought directly and is also classified as hard currency
lifecycle: Effective across all lifecycle stages once the earning path exists. Most visible once a user has enough of a balance to face a real spending choice.
